message.content: **Summary:** I researched Apple's fiscal Q4 2024 results (quarter ended Sept 28, 2024), which Apple reported in late October: quarterly revenue of $94.9 billion, up 6% year over year, and full-year FY2024 net sales of $391.0 billion with net income of $93.7 billion, or $6.08 per diluted share (including a one-time $10.2 billion tax charge) — a record revenue year with steady growth, and news flow describing shares as steady around $222 as investors weigh iPhone 16 demand and the Apple Intelligence rollout, i.e., a fairly valued, unremarkable setup rather than a catalyst-driven spike. One search result claimed Nasdaq had halted AAPL all day under "rule T12," but that came from an unofficial site (nasdaq-halts.net) and is contradicted by the live broker quote — a tight $222.68/$222.72 bid-ask with a current timestamp — so I disregarded it rather than letting a dubious page drive the decision. Given solid results and a quote near $222.70, I bought 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.80, which filled at $222.80 for roughly $9,803 — within the $10,000 per-order cap and well under the $20,000 daily cap. No money was moved out of the account, and only AAPL was traded.
